clients.subOauth: Paste the URL and authorize. No API key needed.

claude.step1: In claude.ai or Claude Desktop, open Settings → Connectors.
claude.step3: Paste the URL above as the connector URL, then click "Add".
claude.step4: Click "Connect" and sign in with mcpemails to authorize. No API key needed.

chatgpt.step1: Open Settings → Apps & Connectors → Advanced settings and turn on Developer mode.
chatgpt.step3: Enter a name and paste the URL above as the Connector URL.
chatgpt.step4: Pick OAuth, click "Create", then authorize with mcpemails.
chatgpt.note: Full MCP is a beta limited to ChatGPT Business and Enterprise/Edu workspaces.

cursor.step3: Cursor prompts you to sign in via OAuth. Authorize with mcpemails.

vscode.step1: Open the Command Palette (⇧⌘P) and run "MCP: Add Server".
vscode.step2: Choose "HTTP", paste the URL above, and give it a name.
vscode.step3: Start the server from the MCP view and authorize when prompted.

cline.step1: In the Cline panel, click the MCP Servers icon, then open the "Remote Servers" tab.
cline.step2: Enter a name and paste the URL above.
cline.step3: Set Transport Type to "Streamable HTTP", then click "Add Server".
cline.step4: Add an "Authorization: Bearer <key>" header using your API key.

windsurf.step1: Open Cascade’s MCP settings, or edit ~/.codeium/windsurf/mcp_config.json.
windsurf.step2: Add the server below. Note the field is "serverUrl", not "url".
windsurf.step3: Refresh MCP servers in Cascade and authorize with mcpemails when prompted.

gemini.step2: Add the server below under "mcpServers" using the "httpUrl" field.
gemini.step3: On first connect the CLI auto-discovers OAuth and opens the browser flow.

zed.step1: In the Agent Panel settings click "Add Custom Server", or edit settings.json.
zed.step3: Zed prompts the OAuth flow when no Authorization header is set. Sign in with mcpemails.

jetbrains.step1: Open Settings → Tools → AI Assistant → Model Context Protocol (MCP).
jetbrains.step2: Click "Add" and select "Streamable HTTP" as the connection type.
jetbrains.step3: Paste the URL above, then add an "Authorization: Bearer <key>" header with your API key.

raycast.step1: Run the "Install MCP Server" command (or "Manage MCP Servers").
raycast.step2: Enter a name, set Transport to "HTTP", and paste the URL above.
raycast.step3: Press "Install MCP Server", then click "Sign In" to authorize with mcpemails.

warp.step1: Open Settings → Agents → MCP servers and click "+ Add".
warp.step2: Select the "Streamable HTTP or SSE Server (URL)" tab.
warp.step3: Paste the URL above and confirm, then complete browser OAuth when prompted.

api.step1: Create an API key in Dashboard → API Keys, then copy it (shown only once).
api.step2: Send requests to the URL above with an Authorization: Bearer header.

review.title: Approve this email before it is sent
review.titleSettled: This send has already been decided
review.subtitle: An AI assistant prepared this email. It has not been delivered, and it will only be sent if you approve it here.
review.subject: Subject
review.recipientsAtSend: This page could not read the recipients from the original message. They will be resolved when it is sent, so check the message text before approving.
review.bccCount: {count, plural, one {# hidden recipient} other {# hidden recipients}}
review.bodyTruncated: This message is longer than 64 KB and has been clipped here. Open it in the dashboard to read all of it.
review.bodyWithheldRole: The message text is shown to workspace owners, admins and members. Your role can review the delivery details only.
review.bodyStoredWithProvider: This request sends a draft that is stored with your email provider, so the text is not part of the request. Open the draft in your mail app to read it before deciding.
review.bodyDecryptFailed: The stored message could not be decrypted, so it cannot be shown. Reject this request and ask your assistant to prepare it again.
review.bodyAbsent: This request has no message text.
review.bodyHtmlNote: The HTML version is shown as source and never rendered. Rendering it would load remote images, which would tell whoever composed this message when and where you opened this page.
review.readOnly: You can review this send, but only a workspace owner or admin can approve or reject it.
review.footnote: Approving is possible only from this page, signed in as a workspace owner or admin. An assistant can prepare a send and can reject one, but it has no browser session, so it cannot approve one.
review.backToConversation: You can close this tab and go back to your conversation.
review.notFoundBody: The link may be out of date, or it may belong to a workspace you are not a member of. Check that you are signed in with the right account.

caveats.outlookSentItems: A copy is written to Sent Items automatically.

errors.generic: That decision could not be recorded. Nothing was sent. Please try again.

mode.label: Review before sending
mode.offHint: The assistant sends without asking. The right choice for an inbox you use for low-stakes mail.
mode.inlineHint: A card appears in the AI conversation showing exactly what will be sent. You can reject it there; approving opens a page you have to be signed in to use.
mode.dashboardHint: No card in the conversation. The assistant is told the send is waiting, and you decide here.
mode.guarantee: In both review modes the email is prepared but not delivered. Approving happens only in a signed-in browser session held by a workspace owner or admin, which the assistant does not have. The review card is a convenience, not a permission boundary.

trust.headline: Automations never delete email.
trust.neverDeletes: They can only move, label or mark mail as read, and every change is recorded message by message.
trust.forwardApproval: Forwarding always waits for a person to approve it, and a reply is only ever saved as a draft.

modal.createSub: Automations are created switched off. Preview what the filter matches, then turn it on when you are happy.
modal.editSub: Changes take effect from the next scheduled run.
modal.keyHelp: The automation acts as this key, so its runs are metered and logged exactly like a call from your assistant. Revoking the key stops the automation.
modal.maxHelp: Caps how much mail a single run can touch.
modal.filterHelp: Only messages matching every condition you set are acted on. Nothing is interpreted by a model: the filter is a plain search.
modal.previewHelp: Runs this filter against the mailbox right now and changes nothing.
modal.previewFailed: Could not preview this filter against the mailbox.
modal.previewEmpty: Nothing matches this filter right now.
modal.previewCount: {count, plural, =1 {1 message matches right now.} other {# messages match right now.}}
modal.markReadNote: Matching messages are marked as read and left where they are.
modal.forwardToHelp: Separate several addresses with commas. Ten at most.
modal.forwardApprovalNote: Forwarding never happens on its own. Every forward waits under Approvals until a person approves it.
modal.templatePlaceholder: Thanks for getting in touch. Someone will reply shortly.
modal.templateHelp: Saved as a draft, never sent. Placeholders written in double curly braces are filled in: sender_name, sender_email, subject, date. Everything else is literal text.
modal.createdNote: The automation is created switched off. Nothing runs until you turn it on.
